correctness.rationale: For each block its row and column intervals have the same length; ordinary matrix multiplication is nonzero exactly when the first column interval and second row interval meet. The zero-product gap count has two left/right orders, three slack gaps, and independent unused interval starts. The resulting sum is polynomial of degree at most six by expansion into monomials and summation in s, so the seven exact values in RESULT.md really prove the identity. Independently, classify nonempty intersections by their first position i. The weighted count of intervals starting at i is A=(n-i+1)(n+i)/2; the weighted count containing i is C=(n+1)i(n-i+1)/2, since the free other start contributes n+start-end and averaging over the rectangle of endpoints gives (n+1)/2. At least one interval starts at i, so sum A(2C-A) over i=1..n. Expanding and using power sums gives n(n+1)(7n^4+14n^3+21n^2+14n+4)/120, the claimed expression. Subtracting 2Q_n-1 removes identity pairs exactly; leading terms (7/120)n^6 and (1/9)n^6 give 21/40. The n=1 extension also gives 1 for the product count, without asserting a ratio on an empty nonzero set. Independent replay `python3 /workspace/reproductions/review_2.py` checks explicit interval sets and first overlaps at n=1..10 (17, 118, 514 for n=2,3,4). This finite run supports, not replaces, the symbolic count.
residual_risks: No formal proof or external attestation is claimed.
